story: Copying the next token of a formulaic multi-token template (map listing headers, markdown reference links, repeated checklist prefixes) that already occurred verbatim earlier in the same document.
Emitting the next subword piece that completes a long word already in progress (place names, technical terms, section markers), i.e. a non-space continuation token rather than a new word.

Reproducing the next token of a local pattern that appeared earlier in the context - whitespace runs, separators, and word pieces are all continued by copying the token that followed the same prefix before.
Predicting the space-prefixed closed-class word (article, pronoun, conjunction) that opens the next phrase in flowing prose.
Placing the comma or period that closes a clause or sentence in running prose, in both travel-guide and technical/news text.
Continuing structured list-like or directory-like lines (addresses, headers, name sequences) by copying the token that followed the same pattern earlier in the document.
Completing a noun phrase: either attaching a common inflectional/derivational suffix (-s, -ed, -ation) to an unfinished word or supplying the space-prefixed head noun it sets up.
Emitting the sentence-final period (or clause-final comma) at the natural end of a complete statement, regardless of topic.
unclear
Terminating a finished line or sentence: the period that ends a statement or the newline that ends a completed line (prose sentence, code statement, heading block).
Predicting the space-prefixed grammatical connector (copula, auxiliary, or preposition such as 'is', 'are', 'to', 'of') that links a noun phrase to what follows.
Completing the second half of a hyphenated or compound word (or an otherwise split word) with its next lowercase subword piece.
Attaching the possessive/contraction 's (apostrophe forms) to a noun or proper name that has just been mentioned.
Continuing highly repetitive boilerplate token sequences (URL fragments, whitespace/padding runs, template headers) by repeating what followed the same sequence earlier in the document.
The newline that immediately follows a sentence-ending period at the end of a paragraph line, in any kind of document.
Emitting the next subword piece of an unusual multi-token word or proper name (rare place names, technical coinages, foreign words).
Supplying the linking token inside an enumeration or range - the comma between items or the 'to'/'of' joining paired elements ('from X to Y', 'ranging from A to B').
Predicting the space-prefixed next word that continues a long descriptive sentence mid-flow, most often a preposition, conjunction, or the noun the sentence structure demands.
After a verb of having/being ('has', 'have', 'is', 'are', 'there's'), predicting the determiner or copula that introduces the following noun phrase.
Continuing a rare proper name or foreign/technical word with its next non-initial subword piece (names of people, places, classes in code).
